about: Teaching rules distilled from bridge bidding net D (D_cw_s75k, stage D5OWN4XC). situations.advise(calls, dealer, seat, hand, rules) applies them.

schema.rules: ordered list; the FIRST rule whose `situation` matches owns the decision
schema.rules[].situation: conditions on the features below (all must hold)
schema.rules[].branches: ordered; the first branch whose `when` holds and whose action is possible gives the call
schema.condition: feature: [lo, hi] inclusive numeric range (null = open) | string or bool equality | list of strings (membership); special keys: 'any': [conditions, ...] (one must hold), 'not': conditions
schema.do.level: min = cheapest legal bid in that strain; jump = one level higher; game = 3NT/4M/5m (or cheapest if above); slam = 6-level; an integer = that exact level. Strain: support = the partner suit I hold most of; rebid = my longest bid suit; new_suit = see situations._pick_new_suit; their_suit = their last suit
schema.stats: measured on held-out self-play: situation_share / coverage = share of all post-opening decisions; agree_call = exact call agreement with D; agree_type = same action type; branch d_does = D's action labels in that branch; hcp_when_agree = 10th-90th pct HCP where rule and D agree
schema.sayc: rules[].sayc / branches[].sayc / core_ideas / habits / sayc_differences: how Standard American Yellow Card treats the same spot, and where D differs (teaching text only; a branch without `sayc` has no note)
schema.call_meanings: what a call showed: HCP of D's hands making it (lo = 10th pct, mid = median, hi = 90th pct), keyed 'situation|action' as returned by situations.call_keys()

features.we_opened: our side made the first bid
features.rho: right-hand opponent's last call: pass / bid / double / redouble / none
features.contested: the other side has made a non-pass call
features.opp_bids: number of bids (not passes or doubles) by the opponents
features.level: level of the current contract (0 = none)
features.owner: who holds the current contract: us / them
features.doubled: current contract is doubled (1) or redoubled (2)
features.game_reached: current contract is at game level or higher (3NT, 4H/4S, 5C/5D)
features.fit: partner and I have both bid the same suit
features.partner_last: action label of partner's last informative call (e.g. support_min, nt_min, pass)
features.partner_key: meaning key 'situation|action' of partner's last informative call
features.partner_last_type: type of partner's last informative call: support / new_suit / rebid / nt / pass / double / their_suit
features.partner_last_level: level kind of partner's last call: min / jump / game / slam / ''
features.partner_raised_me: partner's last suit bid was in a suit I bid first or also bid
features.partner_lo: HCP partner has shown: 10th percentile of D's hands for that call
features.my_shown: median HCP D holds for my own last informative call (what partner thinks I have)
features.hcp: high card points (A4 K3 Q2 J1)
features.support: my length in partner's suit (the partner suit I hold most of)
features.own_len: length of my longest suit that I have already bid
features.new_len: length of the new suit I would bid (see _pick_new_suit)
features.new_level: level at which that new suit would be bid (0 = none possible)
features.suit_margin: suit test: HCP + 3 x new_len - (18 + 3 x new_level); >= 0 passes
features.their_len: my length in the opponents' last bid suit (-1 = they bid no suit)
features.their_hcp: my HCP in the opponents' last bid suit
features.their_stopper: A, Kx, Qxx or Jxxx in the opponents' last bid suit
features.fit_cards: most cards partner and I hold together in one of partner's suits (partner counted 4 per suit, +1 per rebid, 3 for raising mine)
features.extra: hcp - my_shown (points beyond what I have already shown)

situations.R_1suit: Partner opened one of a suit; my first turn
situations.R_1NT: Partner opened 1NT (strong, any shape); my first turn
situations.O_rebid: I opened, partner has bid; my second turn
situations.O_alone: I opened, partner only passed, opponents compete; my second turn
situations.R_rebid: Partner opened, I have had one turn; my second turn
situations.WE_later: We opened; my third turn or later
situations.D_direct: Right-hand opponent opened; my first turn
situations.D_lho: Left-hand opponent opened, partner passed; my first turn
situations.D_advance: They opened, partner has bid or doubled, I have not bid yet
situations.D_silent: They opened, neither partner nor I have bid, my second turn or later
situations.D_later: They opened, I have already bid or doubled

rules.title: We are already in game: stop, or bid a slam
rules.when: Our side holds the contract and it is already a game (3NT, 4 of a major, 5 of a minor) or higher.
rules.think: The job is done: game is where most of D's points come from, and D almost never looks for slam with careful asking bids. Pass unless one of two things is true: partner has just shown slam interest at the 5-level, or 3NT is the wrong game because you hold a long suit and a singleton.
rules.notes: Slam bidding is D's weakest spot for rules: at the 4-level D sometimes jumps straight to slam with 30+ combined, with no asking bid first. No rule here catches that.
rules.sayc: Slams in SAYC are bid with asking bids: Blackwood 4NT asks for aces (5NT for kings), Gerber 4C over a notrump opening. D has no asking bids and jumps to slam on combined strength.

branches.say: Partner bid notrump at the 4- or 5-level: that asks you to choose a slam. With a 6-card suit bid 6 of it
branches.sayc: 4NT is Blackwood in SAYC (it asks how many aces you hold, answered by steps), or a natural slam invitation after notrump. D differs.

branches.say: ... otherwise bid 6NT
At the 5-level with a fit and 29+ points together: bid the slam
branches.sayc: SAYC wants about 33 points together for a small slam and checks aces with Blackwood first. D bids slam lighter.

branches.say: Partner keeps bidding new suits at the 5-level and you have 26+ together: slam
We are in 3NT but you have an 8-card fit and a short suit: move to 4 of the major (5 of a minor)
branches.sayc: Similar in SAYC for a major fit; moving from 3NT to 5 of a minor is rare in SAYC.

branches.say: We are in 3NT but you have a 6-card suit and a singleton or void: play in your suit
Otherwise pass: game is reached
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC.

rules.title: They are in game: pass, double, or bid on
rules.when: The opponents hold the contract at game level or higher.
rules.think: Defend. D bids on over their game only with a huge fit, and doubles only when they have climbed above our own game (a sacrifice) and our side has the points.
rules.notes: With 24-27 together against their 4-level game D is split three ways (pass ~40%, bid 5 ~27%, double ~26%): that is judgment, not a rule.
rules.sayc: Same in SAYC: defend against their game; bidding on (a sacrifice) or doubling is judgment, and vulnerability matters a lot.

branches.say: They bid 5 or more over our game and we hold 24+ together: double
A 10-card fit: bid one more (5 over their 4)
Otherwise pass
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC.

rules.title: Answering partner's one-of-a-suit opening
rules.when: Partner opened 1C/1D/1H/1S and this is your first turn (the opponent on your right may have bid).
rules.think: Partner has 8-16 HCP (usually about 12) and 4+ cards in the suit, 5+ two times out of three. Your first question: do I have a strong hand (13+)? Then say so with notrump. Otherwise: do we have a fit (3+ cards, better 4+)? Raise. No fit: show your own suit, cheaply. D prefers showing a 4-card suit at the 1-level to raising with only 3 cards.
rules.notes: Game raises (1H-4H) are rare: with 4+ support and 13+ D bids 1NT first; after an overcall it splits between the jump raise, game and 2NT. At exactly 12 HCP D is about half 1NT, half a suit bid.
rules.sayc: In SAYC: responder with 6-10 raises a major with 3+ cards, bids a 4-card suit at the 1-level, or bids 1NT (6-10, no fit, not forcing); 10-12 with support makes a limit raise (1H-3H); 13+ bids a new suit (forcing) and heads for game. After an overcall, double is negative (takeout). D differs most on 1NT (13+ any shape, forcing) and on the double.

branches.say: 13+ HCP: bid 1NT = 'I have a strong hand, any shape'. Your suits come later
branches.sayc: 1NT is 6-10, no fit, not forcing in SAYC. With 13+ you bid a new suit (forcing) and make sure of game later. D differs.

branches.say: 4+ card support and 11-12 HCP: jump raise (1H-3H)
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC without competition: a jump raise is a limit raise, 10-12 with support.

branches.say: 6+ HCP and a 4-card suit you can bid at the 1-level: bid it (even with 3-card support)
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC without a fit. With 3+ cards for partner's major and 6-10, SAYC raises instead.

branches.say: A 5-card suit you can bid at the 1-level: bid it, even with very few points
branches.sayc: A new suit needs 6+ HCP in SAYC; with less you pass. D differs.

branches.say: 4+ card support: simple raise (6-10 HCP; if they overcalled, raise with any strength)
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC for 6-10. After an overcall SAYC raises a little lighter too, but not with nothing.

branches.say: 3-card support and 8-12 HCP: simple raise
branches.sayc: 3 cards are enough to raise a major in SAYC (6-10); with 10-12 you make a limit raise instead. A minor is usually raised with 4-5 cards.

branches.say: They overcalled: raise with 3-card support from 7 HCP
They overcalled at the 2-level, you have 11+ but no fit and no long suit: double ('we have the points')
branches.sayc: In SAYC this double is negative: takeout, showing the unbid suit(s). D's double says 'we have the points'.

branches.say: 12 HCP and no fit: also 1NT
branches.sayc: 1NT is 6-10 in SAYC; with 12 you bid a new suit. D differs.

branches.say: No fit: bid your own suit if it passes the suit test (HCP + 3 x length >= 18 + 3 x level)
branches.sayc: SAYC has no suit test: a new suit at the 1-level needs 6+ HCP, at the 2-level 10+ (5 cards for 2H over 1S), and it is forcing.

branches.say: Singleton or void in partner's suit: bid your suit anyway, even with a weak hand
branches.sayc: In SAYC a hand with under 6 HCP passes, whatever its shape (with a long suit it may bid later).

branches.say: Weak and nothing to show: pass
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC (0-5 HCP pass).

rules.title: Answering partner's 1NT opening (strong, any shape)
rules.when: Partner opened 1NT and this is your first turn.
rules.think: 1NT is D's strong opening: 16-22 HCP (usually 18) with any shape, and it is forcing. Never pass it. Your job is to describe: your longest suit, and roughly how many points.
rules.notes: With a 4-card suit and 8-9 HCP D mostly still bids the suit (2-level), sometimes 2NT.
rules.sayc: In SAYC: 1NT is 15-17 and balanced, and responder may pass with 0-7. 2C is Stayman, 2D/2H are Jacoby transfers, 2NT invites (8-9), 3NT is 10-15. D differs: its 1NT is 16-22 any shape and forcing, and every answer is natural.

branches.say: No 5-card suit and 15+: 4NT (slam is close)
branches.sayc: Over a 15-17 1NT, SAYC's 4NT is a natural slam invitation with about 16-17; 3NT covers 10-15.

branches.say: No 5-card suit and 13-14: 3NT
branches.sayc: Same call in SAYC (3NT = 10-15), usually after Stayman when you hold a 4-card major.

branches.say: No 5-card suit and 10-12: 2NT
branches.sayc: In SAYC 2NT invites with 8-9; with 10-12 you bid game. D differs (its 1NT is stronger and wider).

branches.say: A 5-card suit and 10+: jump in it (1NT-3H)
branches.sayc: In SAYC you would start with a Jacoby transfer (majors) and then bid game or 3NT. D bids naturally.

branches.say: A 6+ card suit and 8+: jump in it
branches.sayc: In SAYC you transfer to a major and bid game; with a long minor 3NT is common.

branches.say: Anything weaker (even 0 HCP): bid your longest suit at the 2-level. 2C/2D/2H/2S are natural
branches.sayc: In SAYC 2C is Stayman and 2D/2H are Jacoby transfers; a weak hand with a 5-card major transfers and passes, and a weak balanced hand passes 1NT. D may not pass.

branches.say: They bid over 1NT and you have 8+ without a long suit: double
branches.sayc: Similar in basic SAYC: after they overcall partner's 1NT, double is for penalty.

branches.say: They bid over 1NT: show a decent suit
They bid and you have nothing to add: pass

rules.title: Opener: partner raised my suit
rules.when: You opened one of a suit and partner raised it.
rules.think: A simple raise shows about 4-11 HCP (usually 8) and 3+ cards, often 4. A jump raise shows about 12. The fit is found; the only question is the level. Add your HCP to partner's and look at your trump length: extra trumps are extra tricks.
rules.notes: After a simple raise D rarely jumps straight to game; it bids once more and lets partner decide (about 15-25% of these hands go to game directly).
rules.sayc: Same idea in SAYC: add your points to partner's. A single raise shows 6-10 (3+ for a major); pass with 12-15, invite with 16-18, bid game with 19+. A limit raise (10-12) is accepted with more than a minimum. D's openings and raises are lighter.

branches.say: After a jump raise, with only 4 trumps and 11+: 3NT
branches.sayc: A SAYC 1H/1S opening promises 5 cards, so you would bid 4 of the major; 3NT is a choice after a minor-suit raise.

branches.say: After a jump raise, with 5+ trumps and 10+: bid game
branches.sayc: Same idea in SAYC, but openings start at about 12-13, so accept the limit raise with about 14+.

branches.say: After a jump raise with a minimum: pass
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC.

branches.say: Only 4 trumps but 15+: bid notrump at the cheapest level (strong hand)
branches.sayc: In SAYC notrump here would be natural and balanced, not 'strong, any shape'. D differs.

branches.say: 6+ trumps: bid your suit once more
branches.sayc: In SAYC 1H-2H-3H is an invitation (about 16-18 points); a minimum with 6 trumps usually passes.

branches.say: 5 trumps and 12+: bid your suit once more (an invitation)
branches.sayc: Same idea in SAYC, but the invitation shows about 16-18 points.

branches.say: Minimum: pass
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC (12-15 passes a single raise).

rules.title: Opener: partner answered 1NT (strong, any shape)
rules.when: You opened one of a suit and partner answered 1NT (or 2NT over an overcall).
rules.think: Partner's notrump shows 12-18 HCP (usually 14), any shape: game is likely. It is forcing, so describe your hand. Your opening was light, so a minimum (8-12) is normal: show a second suit or rebid a long one. With 13+ say so with 2NT or a jump.
rules.notes: With 13-15 and a second 5-card suit D is split between a simple and a jump bid in the new suit (about 40/40). With 13-15 and no second suit D bids 2NT only about half the time; the rest are suit bids.
rules.sayc: In SAYC: partner's 1NT answer is 6-10 and not forcing: pass with a balanced minimum, rebid a 6-card suit, or show a second suit; only extra strength (about 16+) invites game. D differs: its 1NT answer is 12-18 and forcing.

branches.say: They bid into our strength and you have 11+: double (they are outgunned)
They bid: rebid a 6-card suit
They bid: show a 5-card second suit
They bid and you are minimum: pass, partner will act
6-card suit and 11+: jump in it
branches.sayc: In SAYC a jump rebid (1H-1NT-3H) shows 16-18 and a good 6-card suit (invitational).

branches.say: 6-card suit, minimum: rebid it
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC.

branches.say: 16+ without a 5-card side suit: 3NT
13+ and a 5-card second suit: jump in it

branches.sayc: In SAYC 2NT here invites game with about 18-19 balanced; 13-15 passes 1NT or rebids naturally.

branches.say: Minimum: show your second suit
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC, as long as the second suit is lower-ranking than your first (not a reverse).

branches.say: Minimum with one suit: rebid it
branches.sayc: In SAYC a balanced minimum passes 1NT; rebidding the suit shows 6 cards.

rules.title: Opener: partner answered in a new suit
rules.when: You opened one of a suit and partner bid a new suit (or doubled).
rules.think: Partner has about 5-12 HCP and 4+ cards in the new suit (5+ if it was at the 2-level). A new suit is NOT forcing in D's style: with a minimum and nothing to add you may pass. First look for a fit with partner's suit, then show extra strength or a second suit.
rules.notes: With 17+ and a 4-card side suit D is split between the new suit (~40%) and notrump (~40%).
rules.sayc: In SAYC: a new suit by responder is forcing for one round: opener must bid again even with a minimum (raise with 4-card support, 1NT with 12-14 balanced, a second suit, or rebid a 6-card suit). D differs: opener may pass.

branches.say: 4+ cards in partner's suit: raise it once
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC with a minimum (12-15); with 16-18 SAYC jump-raises.

branches.say: 3-card support and 11-15: raise it once
branches.sayc: SAYC usually raises a 1-level major response only with 4 cards; with 3 it rebids 1NT or its own suit.

branches.say: 15-16, no fit: notrump at the cheapest level
branches.sayc: In SAYC a 1NT rebid is 12-14 balanced (15-17 balanced would have opened 1NT); 18-19 jumps to 2NT. D differs.

branches.say: A 5-card second suit: bid it (any strength)
branches.sayc: Similar in SAYC, but a second suit higher than your first at the 2-level (a reverse) needs about 17+.

branches.say: 17+ with a second suit: bid it
17+ without a second suit: notrump
branches.sayc: In SAYC 18-19 balanced jumps to 2NT here.

branches.say: 6-card suit: rebid it
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC (12-15; a jump rebid shows 16-18).

branches.say: Minimum, no fit, nothing new: pass (partner's suit is a fine spot)
branches.sayc: Not in SAYC: a new-suit response is forcing, so opener rebids 1NT, the own suit, or a cheap second suit. D differs.

rules.title: Opener: partner passed and the opponents compete
rules.when: You opened, partner passed, and the opponents are bidding.
rules.think: Partner's pass says 0-9 HCP and no fit worth showing. Do not fight for the contract on your own unless your hand is long or strong.
rules.notes: With a 5-card suit and 12-17 D competes about one time in three.
rules.sayc: Similar in SAYC: after partner passes, opener competes only with extra length or strength. With shortness in their suit a SAYC opener also reopens with a takeout double, because partner may be waiting to pass it for penalty.

branches.say: 16+ and 1NT is still available: 1NT shows the strong hand
branches.sayc: In SAYC 1NT here is balanced with a stopper in their suit; a strong unbalanced hand doubles or bids a second suit.

branches.say: A 6+ card suit: rebid it (at the 2-level)
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC.

branches.say: A 7-card suit: rebid it even at the 3-level
17+ and a second suit: bid it
Otherwise pass
branches.sayc: SAYC opener more often reopens with a takeout double when short in their suit.

rules.title: They opened: overcall, notrump, or pass
rules.when: An opponent opened and this is your first chance to bid (partner has passed or not yet spoken).
rules.think: Overcall whenever you have a good suit: that is D's main weapon, it takes away the opponents' room and tells partner what to lead. The test is the suit test: HCP + 3 x length of your suit must reach 18 + 3 x the level you bid at (21 at the 1-level, 24 at the 2-level, 27 at the 3-level). A strong hand bids notrump instead (strong, any shape), not double: D almost never makes a takeout double.
rules.notes: Examples of the suit test at the 1-level: a 4-card suit needs 9 HCP, a 5-card suit 6, a 6-card suit 3. At the 2-level: 5-card 9 HCP, 6-card 6 HCP. D sometimes jumps with a 6-7 card suit and 10-15 HCP; no rule here.
rules.sayc: In SAYC: an overcall shows 8-16 HCP and a good 5+ card suit (a 2-level overcall wants a better suit and more points); jump overcalls are weak. A 1NT overcall is 15-18, balanced, with a stopper in their suit. Other strong hands, and opening hands short in their suit, make a takeout double. D differs: it overcalls 4-card suits and long suits with few points, and bids notrump instead of doubling.

branches.say: 18+: notrump at the cheapest level (strong, any shape)
branches.sayc: SAYC's 1NT overcall is 15-18, balanced, with a stopper; stronger or unbalanced hands double first and bid again. D differs.

branches.say: 15-17 without a suit to show at the 1-level or a 5-card suit: notrump
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC if balanced with a stopper in their suit; otherwise a takeout double (short in their suit).

branches.say: Your suit passes the suit test: bid it (cheapest level)
branches.sayc: SAYC overcalls need about 8-16 HCP and a good 5+ card suit; 4-card overcalls and very light overcalls of long suits are not standard (a long suit with few points makes a weak jump overcall).

branches.say: LHO opened and partner passed: bid your suit only if it passes the suit test by 2 more
Otherwise pass
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC for weak hands; with opening values and shortness in their suit SAYC makes a takeout double.

rules.title: Partner bid over their opening: support, bid, or pass
rules.when: The opponents opened, partner has overcalled (or bid notrump), and you have not bid yet.
rules.think: Partner's overcall shows a real suit (usually 5+) and about 7-15 HCP. With support, raise: the more trumps you have, the higher you may go, even with a weak hand. Without support, only bid your own suit if it is good, or notrump with 12+. If partner bid notrump, partner is strong (14-20, any shape): answer as you would to a 1NT opening.
rules.notes: With 3-card support and the opponents silent D often passes: 62% of the time with 7-9 HCP, 34% with 10-12 (then it raises or bids notrump). With 4+ support and 13+ D bids game about 40% of the time; the rest are cheaper raises or notrump.
rules.sayc: Same idea in SAYC: raise partner's overcall with support, and a new suit is not forcing. A strong raise starts with a cue-bid of their suit. Notrump shows a stopper in their suit. A 1NT overcall (15-18 balanced) is answered much like a 1NT opening.

branches.say: Partner's notrump, 10+ and a 5-card suit: jump in your suit
Partner's notrump, 9+ and no long suit: raise notrump
Partner's notrump, weaker: bid your longest suit
branches.sayc: In SAYC a weak hand may pass partner's 1NT overcall (15-18 balanced). D's notrump is forcing.

branches.say: Partner's notrump and they bid again: double with 7+
Partner's notrump and they bid again: show a 5-card suit
4+ support and 13+: bid game
branches.sayc: In SAYC a strong raise usually starts with a cue-bid of their suit.

branches.say: 4+ support: raise once, whatever your strength
branches.sayc: Similar in SAYC: raise with 3+ support and about 6-10; a very weak hand raises only with a long fit.

branches.say: 3-card support, 6+, and they bid again: raise
12+ without a fit: notrump (strong)
branches.sayc: In SAYC notrump here is natural with a stopper in their suit, and not forcing. D's notrump is strong and forcing.

branches.say: Short in partner's suit: bid your own suit if it nearly passes the suit test
Doubleton in partner's suit: bid your suit if it passes the suit test
Otherwise pass
branches.sayc: Same in SAYC.

rules.title: Partner and I have both passed: stay out
rules.when: They opened; you and partner have only passed so far.
rules.think: You passed once already, so your hand did not pass the suit test, and partner's did not either. D does not come in late ('balance'): keep passing.
rules.notes: About 3% of the time D bids a long suit late; no simple rule predicts it.
rules.sayc: SAYC does balance: after 1X-P-P (or when they stop low) the last player may overcall or double with a few points less than usual. D does not.

branches.say: Pass

rules.title: They outbid us below game: compete or pass
rules.when: Any later turn: the opponents hold the contract below game.
rules.think: Compete only with a fit. Count the cards you and partner hold together in the suit (partner promised 4 for a suit bid once, 5 for a suit bid twice, 3 for a raise of yours). 8+ cards together, full values for what you have shown, and a short suit: bid one more. No fit: let them play, unless you have a very long suit.
rules.notes: 'Full values' = at least the HCP your earlier bids promised (see the table of what calls show). D doubles them only rarely here (about 2%).
rules.sayc: Similar in SAYC: compete with a known 8+ card fit, usually one level at a time, and let them play without one. A double here is more often for takeout than in D's style.

branches.say: 8+ card fit, a singleton or void, and full values: bid one more
8+ card fit and full values, still at the 2-level: bid one more
10-card fit: bid one more
A 7-card suit: rebid it
23+ together and a new 5-card suit: bid it
Otherwise pass

rules.title: Partner raised my suit (later rounds): game or not
rules.when: Our contract below game, and partner's last bid supported a suit you bid.
rules.think: The fit is agreed; decide the level. A raise to the 3-level without competition is an invitation: D accepts almost always. In a competitive auction go to game with extra values and shape.
rules.notes: In a 3-level fight with 2-6 extra points D is split between game, 3NT and pass: judgment.
rules.sayc: Same idea in SAYC: a 3-level raise without competition invites game. SAYC accepts only with a non-minimum; D accepts almost always.

branches.say: Partner invited at the 3-level (no competition): bid game
... with a balanced hand: 3NT
They compete at the 3-level, 22+ together and some shape: bid game
23+ together and 5+ trumps: bid one more
Otherwise pass

rules.title: Partner bid notrump (strong, any shape) in a later round
rules.when: Our contract below game, and partner's last bid was notrump.
rules.think: Partner's notrump is strong and forcing, just like the 1NT opening. Do not pass below game: show a fit, 3NT with a balanced hand, or keep describing your shape.
rules.sayc: In SAYC notrump rebids are natural, balanced and limited (1NT rebid 12-14, jump to 2NT 18-19) and partner may pass below game. D's notrump is strong, any shape and forcing.

branches.say: 8-card fit and an unbalanced hand: show the fit
Balanced: 3NT
A 6-card suit: rebid it
Another 4-card suit: show it
A 5-card suit: rebid it
Otherwise: notrump at the cheapest level

rules.title: Our auction, below game: place the contract
rules.when: Any other later turn with our side holding the contract below game.
rules.think: Add your HCP to what partner has shown (table below): 25+ together is game. Play in an 8-card fit if there is one, otherwise in notrump. D stops low readily: with nothing more to say, pass.
rules.notes: This is the weakest rule (about 45% agreement): later-round decisions depend on the exact auction in ways no short rule captures. D's other choices here are spread over 3NT, preference bids, and new suits.
rules.sayc: Same idea in SAYC: about 25-26 points together for game, an 8-card major fit first, otherwise notrump.

branches.say: At the 3-level with an 8-card fit: bid game
At the 3-level without a fit, 23+ together: 3NT
A fit and 26+ together: show the fit
A 5-card suit not shown yet: bid it
Nothing more to say: pass

core_ideas.name: Count HCP; about 25 together is game
core_ideas.sayc: Same idea in SAYC: about 25-26 points together for game (HCP plus shape), but about 33 for a small slam, checked with Blackwood first. D bids slam lighter (29-30 with a fit).

core_ideas.name: 1NT means strong hand, any shape
core_ideas.sayc: 1NT is balanced and limited in SAYC: an opening shows 15-17 (strong unbalanced hands open one of a suit or 2C), a response 6-10 and not forcing, an overcall 15-18 with a stopper in their suit. D differs completely.

core_ideas.name: Every suit bid is natural
core_ideas.sayc: Mostly natural too, but SAYC adds artificial calls D does not use: the strong 2C opening, Stayman and Jacoby transfers over 1NT, Blackwood, takeout and negative doubles, and cue-bids of the opponents' suit (which show strength, not length). 1C/1D may be a 3-card suit.

core_ideas.name: A fit is 8+ cards together
core_ideas.sayc: Same in SAYC. The promises differ a little: 1H/1S openings show 5+, 1C/1D can be 3, a new suit by responder shows 4+.

core_ideas.name: The suit test
core_ideas.sayc: SAYC has no single formula: an overcall shows about 8-16 HCP and a good 5+ card suit; a response in a new suit needs 6+ HCP at the 1-level and 10+ at the 2-level. D overcalls 4-card suits (9+ HCP) and long suits with very few points.

core_ideas.name: Which suit to bid
core_ideas.sayc: Largely the same in SAYC: longest suit first, with two 5-card suits the higher, 4-card suits up the line at the 1-level. With 10+ a SAYC responder bids a longer suit first, even at the 2-level.

habits.name: A new suit is not forcing
habits.sayc: The reverse in SAYC: a new suit by responder is forcing for one round (a jump shift forces to game), while notrump bids are natural, balanced and limited. 2-over-1 is forcing for one round, not to game. D differs.

habits.name: Doubles are rare
habits.sayc: SAYC doubles a lot: a takeout double of their opening (opening values, short in their suit, or any strong hand), negative doubles after they overcall. Low-level penalty doubles are rare in both. D differs.

habits.name: D stops low and does not balance
habits.sayc: SAYC balances: after 1X-P-P, or when they stop at a low level, the last player may double or overcall with a few points less than usual. D differs.

sayc_differences: **1NT.** SAYC: 15-17 balanced opening, 6-10 non-forcing response, 15-18 overcall with a stopper. D: 'strong hand, any shape' (opening 16-22, response 12-18, overcall 14-20) and forcing.
**What is forcing.** SAYC: a new suit by responder is forcing, notrump bids are limited. D: the other way round; a new suit may be passed, notrump may not.
**Doubles.** SAYC uses takeout and negative doubles all the time. D almost never doubles (1.5% of calls) and a strong hand over their opening bids notrump.
**Conventions.** SAYC has a strong 2C, weak twos, Stayman, Jacoby transfers, Blackwood and cue-bids. D bids naturally and has no asking bids, even for slam.

**Strength.** SAYC opens with about 12+ and overcalls with 8-16 and a good 5-card suit, and balances. D opens with 8-16, overcalls by the suit test (4-card suits, very light long suits) and does not balance.
